def test_a_missing_origin_main_skips_silently(root, capsys, publish_upstream):
    """A fresh clone, an offline machine, a CI checkout that fetched only the branch."""
    branch_off(root, publish_upstream)
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root.parent), "update-ref", "-d", "refs/remotes/origin/main"], check=True
    )
    was = root / "decisions" / "accepted" / "0002-beta.md"
findings.message: subprocess module calls execute external commands. Without careful input validation, this enables command injection.
findings.remediation: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and an explicit argument list. Validate all inputs and avoid passing user-controlled data to commands.

findings.message: Large whitespace padding was detected (a block of blank lines or a long run of spaces). This can push injected instructions below or to the right of the visible area so a human reviewer never sees them while the agent still reads them. Manual review of the hidden content is recommended.
findings.remediation: Remove the large whitespace padding (blank-line blocks or long space runs) and review any content hidden below or to the right of it. Keep skill files compact and reviewable so no instructions can be concealed off-screen.

| only **dereferenceable** refs         | refuses; re-run `promote <name…> --deref` (shows the moves)                                                       |

findings.message: Dependencies lack version pinning, allowing potential malicious package updates. Consider pinning versions.
findings.remediation: Pin all dependency versions in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml. Use exact versions (==) or compatible ranges. Run pip-audit regularly.

findings.message: Dependency has known vulnerabilities (CVEs). Using packages with unpatched security flaws exposes the environment to known exploits.
findings.pattern: Unverifiable Dependency: pytest has 2 known advisory(ies) (CVE-2025-71176 (pytest has vulnerable tmpdir handling); CVE-2025-71176 (pytest has vulnerable tmpdir handling)), but the manifest does not pin a version, so it is unknown whether the installed release is affected
findings.remediation: Update the dependency to a patched version that addresses the known CVE. Check OSV (osv.dev) or NVD for details on the vulnerability.
